1	# Nexus Code v1.1.4 Plan
2	
3	**Status:** Plan and owner decisions recorded (section 6); execution starts when this PR merges. **Base:** `main` at v1.1.3 (published 2026-11-05, `46fd5045`).
4	**Scope (owner, 2026-11-04):** (1) resolve every open finding from the v1.1.2 source (shipped as v1.1.3); (2) add Worktrunk functionality in the best-integrated way.
5	
6	## 1. Principles
7	
8	- Close findings with the fix first, the regression test red first, and an independent review per work package. Findings are closed with evidence, never by editing the finding.
9	- No new runtime dependency (gate G1.1-5: zero deprecated packages, `cargo deny`, SBOM, notices). Anything Worktrunk-shaped must be built on Node, git and the system `cp`.
10	- Project-supplied commands are untrusted input. Nothing a repository file declares runs without an approval that lives outside the repository.
11	- One exact-head gate per release candidate, run with the CI fixture variables set so `make test` runs through, in a clean worktree with its own `npm ci`.
12	
13	## 2. Findings ledger
14	
15	**Numbering.** `WP-1301` to `WP-1308` and `WP-1310` to `WP-1315` below are the v1.1.4 work packages. They supersede the same IDs in `docs/v1.1.0/ROADMAP.md` (OTLP exporter, provenance graph, macOS builds, knowledge freshness, cgroup limits, Composio mesh), which were never scheduled. Those roadmap items keep their own IDs only inside that document; in commits, claims and findings, `WP-13xx` means this plan. If one of them is scheduled later, give it a new ID.
16	
17	Sources: my independent reviews on PR #402 (WP-1105 evaluators, WP-1107 provider work), Entire trail 145 (15 open findings after the `--step` HIGH was fixed in v1.1.2), Entire trail 140, Entire trail 146, the gate-3 flake recorded in the findings ledger, and the known limitations in `docs/releases/v1.1.2.md` and `docs/releases/v1.1.3.md`. Every item below must end as FIXED (with a test), WITHDRAWN (with evidence it is not a defect) or DEFERRED (owner decision, with a reason). Work packages are ordered by risk.
18	
19	### WP-1301 Single-step mode and the TUI (WP-1106)
20	- TUI `/step` calls `agent.runTurn` directly: no rollback checkpoint, no live tool events, no saved session, a blocked turn reported as success. Dispatch it as a normal sidecar job, `runJob(id, undefined, (signal) => this.turn(...))` as the other turn commands do (`cli/src/sidecar.ts:323`, `:353`, `:454`; the runner is `turn()` at `sidecar.ts:557`), so it gets the checkpoint, observer, saved session and `turn.result`. The REPL `/step` already uses `InteractiveRepl.prepareTurnCheckpoint` and `runInteractiveTurn` (`cli/src/repl.ts:196`, `:212`, `:874-875`), which are private to the REPL and are not what the TUI should call.
21	- `/step` is not `cancellable`.
22	- The step pause overwrites a `STAGNATION_DETECTED` stop and skips `endStep()`; guard on `!stopReason` and call `endStep()` before pausing, so stagnation detection advances across `/step` calls.
23	- Tests: drive the real REPL `/step` handler and the TUI `stepSlash`; the current REPL test re-implements the logic and would pass if the handler were deleted.

25	### WP-1302 Code evaluators (WP-1105)
26	- **Fail-open overlay (HIGH in review):** build and `typecheck_clean` overlay only `.ts .mts .cts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs .jsx .rs .py` candidate files on the baseline. Carry every candidate build input (additions and deletions), or fail closed and report ignored changed paths.
27	- Shadowing through `node_modules` and in-repo build helpers (`build.rs`, `setup.py`, `conftest.py`, `tools/*.js`) that are overlaid as source.
28	- Two full workspace snapshots refuse large `node_modules` (5 s deadline, 50,000 entries).
29	- Evaluator commands have no memory, pid or disk limits; parsers have no timeout (65 MB `.ts` blocked 62.9 s); a command path that resolves outside the workspace through a symlink or `..`.
30	- `typecheck_clean`: coded diagnostics only (document or make the recogniser task-supplied); line-shift false failures; identical recognised config errors (TS5057) pass; `--pretty` output.
31	- `node --check` accepts an ESM-syntax `.js` file that contains a syntax error.
32	- `diff_boundary` counts evaluator-staged hidden tests as agent changes for non-hardened tasks with `hidden.dir` (run evaluators before staging, or snapshot separately).
33	- Candidate edits to build configuration are silently ignored: report them.
34	- Dangling-symlink overlay fails closed with `EEXIST`; pinned workspace under `os.tmpdir()`; `spec.candidate.cwd` overridden; README stale.

36	### WP-1302b Tool-call syntax counting (`cli/src/parser.ts`)
37	Split out of WP-1302 because these items edit `cli/src/parser.ts`, not `eval/`. **Owner: claude-code** (decision 3 gives `eval/` to codex-root and does not cover `cli/`); the `eval/evaluators/code/json_repair_rate.mjs` rows in FINDINGS stay with WP-1302.

43	### WP-1303 Provider handling (WP-1107)
44	- `serverKindCache`: add a TTL, invalidate on endpoint, provider and account switch, key by more than the endpoint string. Fix the gateway-on-404 case that sends `X-Task-Class` to a replaced non-gateway server (REQ-PRV-109 must hold for every path, not only the success path).

46	- A retained vLLM kind keeps `advertised.via` so request counting does not turn off; transient `/version` and Ollama `/api/version` failures must not downgrade a known kind.
47	- Matrix provenance: bind the archive to the verified checkout content, not only to the commit id.
48	- Decide the GBNF compiler: wire it to a consumer (llama.cpp `grammar`, vLLM `guided_json`, Ollama `format`) or remove the dead code. Hybrid reasoning grammars from the v1.1.0 roadmap are still unimplemented.
49	- **Measure G1.1-4** (at least 99.5% valid tool-call JSON across supported provider endpoints) against live endpoints; this needs the shared `GATEWAY` claim. Until measured it stays "not met".

52	### WP-1304 Evaluation CLI, tracing and redaction hygiene
53	- `--isolated-home` is honoured only when `eval` is `argv[0]`; parse after options or reject the flag when it is not applied (currently silently uses the real HOME).
54	- `core-v1/tasks/*` duplicates `eval/tasks/*`, and the evaluator runtime file list exists in two places that already differ.
55	- OTLP scope version is hard-coded `1.1.0`; use `getBuildIdentity().version`.
56	- Sidecar text is redacted per field and again per event (paths corrupted, special case for `session.state`); choose one layer. Four identical diagnostic helpers (`formatCliDiagnostic`, `formatReplDiagnostic`, `formatProviderDiagnostic`, `formatUpgradeDiagnostic`) and `formatSafeSidecarText`: one shared helper next to `redactDiagnosticForOutput`; the REPL step error path skips redaction.
57	- Secret-shaped directory names still appear verbatim in `workspace` and `workspace_name` (known nit).

59	### WP-1305 Release hygiene
60	- Make the CI fixture variables part of the documented local `make test` invocation (or a `make test-ci` target) so a local gate runs through; make `make test` run the terminal-scope and security steps even when the CLI suite fails, or document the abort.
61	- Make the timing-sensitive `agent_observer` test deterministic or give it a bounded retry; the v1.1.3 exact-head gate needed a manual rerun of it.
62	- Keep the findings ledger in `docs/v1.1.4/FINDINGS.md`, updated per closed item with the commit.

64	### WP-1306 Recovered v1.0-era fixes that never reached main
65	Found in the post-v1.1.3 housekeeping (2026-11-05): detached worktrees held 122 commits on no branch. Most of that work is on `main` already (WP-05 egress and secret quarantine, the three checkpoint-restore fixes, corrupt-task listing, credential-store serialisation). The items below were checked against `main` and are **not** in place or only partly. They are anchored on local branches `recovery/orphan-*` and bundled in `~/nexus-archive/housekeeping-20261105/orphan-heads.bundle`. These SHAs, the `recovery/orphan-*` branches, the bundle and `v1/docs-v11-layered-memory` exist only in the owner's local repository; a remote reader cannot check them. Keep the bundle and branches until WP-1306 closes. Port each as a fresh change on `main` (the originals are old rebases), red test first, never a blind cherry-pick.
66	- **Doctor `state.integrity` and message journals** (`recovery/orphan-doctor-journal`: `5be3f6d0`, `7a45c3ab`, `c7028e14`, `c4af6546`, `cf4f2e07`). `cli/src/doctor.ts` validates session and task records but never the schema-2 message journal: a missing committed journal, a future-schema journal and an unreadable one are not distinguished from malformed state, and a large scan cannot be cancelled. Add the journal check with a cancellable worker (`scripts/doctor_message_worker.mjs`, shipped in `dist`), cancellation before repairs and across repair outcomes. Original tests: future journal, unreadable journal, missing committed journal (not quarantined), cancellation terminates a large scan, hanging worker terminated on abort.

Reject a `config.env` that changes `HOME` with a message naming `NEXUS_STATE_DIR`. Red test first to confirm the current behaviour.
68	- **To verify with a red test before porting** (the code on `main` may already cover them in another form; close as WITHDRAWN with evidence if so):
69	  - Session round-trip: `SessionManager.saveSession` (`cli/src/session.ts:109-155`) does not persist `operation`, `providerRecovery` or `changeBaseline` (`89a570f6`, `c1bd29cb`, `2ce6f518`; test "session round-trip preserves operation, provider recovery, and change baseline"). The live resume path probably persists them already: `cli/src/agent.ts:1587-1633` builds the full `DurableTaskState` and calls `saveTaskState` directly, so the gap may be limited to the partial-session `saveSession` path. Decide with a red test (`b733f069`, `eed469dd`).

72	  - Restore mode after a checkpoint-free turn (`cac400ea`; `repl.ts` already resets the fallback, check the sidecar and TUI paths).
73	- Everything else in the orphan set is evidence-doc commits, six 2026-10-05 `wip` commits from the dogfood experiments, and repeated rebases of fixes already on `main`; nothing to port.

75	### WP-1307 Research: review Harness² (issue #69)
76	Tracked in https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/issues/69. It was parked until v1.0.0 shipped; v1 is out, so it is in scope now as **research only**, with no runtime change and no new dependency. Deliverable: `docs/v1.1.4/HARNESS2-REVIEW.md`, an adopt, borrow or skip recommendation per mechanism, answering the five questions in the issue:
77	1. Does contrastive probing without ground truth apply to a Nexus turn, and which behavioural signals would be contrasted?
78	2. How does the eight-component taxonomy (system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, plugins) map onto Nexus context assembly, skills, tool guidance and memory?
79	3. Is the durable "lessons" memory a model for Nexus memory, and how does it avoid drift and over-generalisation?
80	4. Parallel versus sequential recursion budgets against our inference cost profile (gateway-preferred local plus DEC-06 cloud providers).
81	5. Adopt the framework, borrow ideas, or skip?
82	Constraints, carried over from the issue: never run it on held-out T2/T3 tasks (per-task refinement is tuning); a Nexus executor adapter would be needed first and is **out of scope** for v1.1.4; any trial runs inside the Nexus sandbox and network policy (its default is unrestricted network and a disabled Codex sandbox); models only through the gateway or DEC-06 providers; adopted harness edits are candidate changes re-validated on frozen held-out evaluation by someone other than the tuner. Reported gains are the paper's own and unverified. The write-up reads the paper (arXiv 2610.14224) and the Apache-2.0 repository; it does not execute them. It closes the issue only when the write-up merges, and any adopt or borrow item becomes a separate, owner-approved work package for a later release.

84	### WP-1308 Relevance-based skill injection
85	Source: owner report 2026-11-05. On v1.1.3 a single prompt in a repository on a host with 305 installed skills was refused on step 1 (`Context is full`, 59,105 + 8,192 + 4,096 > 65,536): the system prompt advertised every skill with path and full description, 110,548 characters. The immediate defect is fixed in PR #409 (the catalog takes at most 5% of the context window and degrades to shorter descriptions, then names only). At that scale the catalog is names only, so the model chooses a skill by name alone. This package makes the useful descriptions reach the model when they are relevant, without growing the stable prompt.
86	- **Keep the bounded catalog** from PR #409 in the system prompt so the prefix stays byte-stable for local prefix caching (vLLM, llama.cpp).
87	- **Per-turn matching:** score the operator's prompt against each trusted skill's name and description with a local lexical ranker (no model call, no new dependency). When the top scores clear a threshold, add the top 3 to 5 with full descriptions as a system note placed immediately after the newest operator message, never in `messages[0]` and never at a fixed early index. The note is appended to the conversation once, when that operator message arrives, and stays where it was written; it is not re-inserted per request. That keeps every request an append-only extension of the previous one, so the local prefix cache survives each new prompt. This placement differs from the pinned objective, which `requestMessages` (`cli/src/agent.ts`, around line 2711) inserts at index 1 of each request whenever the ledger must be pinned: copying that pattern would put a per-prompt note at the start of the conversation and invalidate the cache on every operator message. The note is bounded by its own share of the window.
88	- **Lookup during the task:** `activate_skill` accepts a query when no skill has that exact name and returns ranked matches (name and description), or a separate read-only `find_skills` tool; whichever adds less tool-schema weight. This covers work that drifts from the opening prompt.
89	- **Trust is unchanged:** matching only advertises a description; it never activates a skill or loads its body. Untrusted workspace skills are never matched or listed. Skill frontmatter grants nothing.
90	- **Tests:** a prompt that names a skill's domain gets that skill's description immediately after that operator message; across two operator messages, the second request starts with the first request's messages unchanged (append-only prefix); an unrelated prompt gets no note; the system prompt is byte-identical across turns with different prompts; a query to `activate_skill` returns ranked matches; untrusted skills never appear; the note stays within its budget with 300+ skills.
91	- **Measure:** report the first-request estimate and the note size on the 305-skill host before and after, and record whether the matched skills for the original citable prompt are plausible.
92	- **Carried from the PR #409 review** (independent ACCEPT at `96bdf612`, low findings left for this package):
93	  - A conversation saved before PR #409 keeps its full catalog in the saved `messages[0]`, because `resizeSkillCatalog` only replaces catalog text it recorded itself. Such a session stays blocked on resume; a new conversation works. Recognise the catalog by its heading and line format when the recorded text is absent, with a test that resumes a pre-#409 session.
94	  - `resizeSkillCatalog` records the new catalog even when the old text was not found in `messages[0]`; record it only after a replacement.
95	  - A catalog that shrank to nothing (windows under about 3K tokens) cannot come back; decide whether it should.
96	  - `getPromptSection` builds the final listing twice; keep it in a variable.
97	  - Test the first-discovery condition and the resume path directly, not only through a full turn.
98	  - The `activate_skill` not-found error lists every skill name; replace it with the ranked lookup above, and update the names-only catalog's "an unknown name passed to `activate_skill` lists them all" hint (`cli/src/skills.ts`) to describe the lookup.

100	## 3. Worktrunk integration
101	
102	### 3.1 What Worktrunk is (survey, 2026-11-04)
103	A Rust CLI `wt` (v0.81.0, pre-1.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0, about 12 releases in 83 days with breaking changes in each). Branch-addressed `switch/list/remove/merge`, a configurable path template (default sibling `repo.branch`), `copy-ignored` build-cache sharing with `.worktreeinclude`, hooks (`pre-start/post-start/pre-merge/...`), per-branch variables, aliases, PR checkout, CI status, LLM commit messages, a picker, and Claude Code and Codex plugins. It shells out to `git`. Its library crate is declared unstable.
104	
105	### 3.2 Decision: native subset first, optional pass-through second
106	| Option | Verdict |
107	|---|---|
108	| A. Adapter only (`wt` on PATH) | Not enough alone: no offline or trust story under Nexus's control, and it only works for users who install `wt`. Kept as phase 2. |
109	| B. Native subset in TypeScript | **Phase 1.** Built on Nexus's own git handling. No dependency, no packaging change. |
110	| C. Embed the `worktrunk` crate | **Rejected.** About 100 new crates, MSRV 1.98, unstable API; breaks G1.1-5 and the SBOM. |
111	| D. Vendor or fork | **Rejected.** Large, fast-moving, and it would tie the release cadence to upstream. |
112	| E. B plus an optional `wt` pass-through | **Chosen.** Phase 2 adds a read-only adapter that detects `wt` by `--version` output. |
113	
114	Licence: reimplementing ideas needs no licence. Do not copy code. Credit Worktrunk in the docs, and do not reuse its name for the feature. The Nexus command is `nexus worktree` (alias `nexus wt` only if no collision is detected at install; `wt` collides with Windows Terminal).
115	
116	### 3.3 Design constraints from the Nexus inventory
117	1. **A new managed worktree kind.** The existing `isManagedWorktreePath` and `hasValidatedOperationGitPaths` accept only `<gitRoot>/.nexus/worktrees/<taskId>` on `nexus/<taskId>`. User-named worktrees at a path template such as `../repo.feature` need their own state kind and validators. Do not loosen the existing ones.
118	2. **Anchor on the git common dir.** The repo root must come from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, not `--show-toplevel`, so Nexus run inside a linked worktree finds the main checkout and sees all siblings. This also fixes a latent bug in `WorktreeManager`.
119	3. **Registry.** Named worktrees are recorded in `<git-common-dir>/nexus/worktrees.json` (atomic write, no symlinks, 64 KiB cap), so `list`, `remove` and state recovery do not depend on the path layout.
120	4. **Safe removal.** `remove` refuses a dirty worktree (including untracked and ignored files) and an unmerged branch unless `--force` / `--delete-unmerged` is given. Do not reuse `WorktreeManager.discardWorktree` (it is `--force` plus `branch -D`).
121	5. **Git hooks off during creation.** Creating a worktree runs `post-checkout`; use the existing `envWithoutConfiguredHooks` suppression (extend it to cover Git 2.54 correctly) for every Nexus-initiated git call.
122	6. **Config without a TOML dependency.** Operator config is JSON (`~/.config/nexus/config.json`, version 1, existing validator). Reading Worktrunk's `.config/wt.toml` and `~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml` uses a small strict TOML-subset reader (tables, strings, string arrays; anything else is an error, never guessed). It is read-only interoperability, not a requirement.
123	7. **Read-only gating in both places.** Every new slash command must be added to `replReadOnlyAllowed` (repl.ts) and `readOnlySlashAllowed` (sidecar.ts) with a test; mutating subcommands are refused in read-only mode.
124	8. **Docs gates.** Fenced `nexus …` examples are executed by `scripts/doc_commands.mjs`; they must parse. Gate 4 scans only top-level `docs/*.md`.
125	
126	### 3.4 Work packages
127	**WP-1310 Core: named worktrees**
128	- `nexus worktree switch <branch> [-c] [--base B] [--no-copy]`, `list [--json]`, `remove <branch>... [--force] [--delete-unmerged]`, `path <branch>`. Branch shortcuts: `^` default branch, `@` current, `-` previous. Accept a worktree path wherever a branch is accepted.
129	- Path template: default `{{ repo_path }}/.nexus/worktrees/{{ branch | sanitize }}` (owner decision 1); the sibling layout `{{ repo_path }}/../{{ repo }}.{{ branch | sanitize }}` is opt-in through a one-time operator config line and is never the default; variables `repo_path`, `repo`, `owner`, `branch`; filters `sanitize`, `hash_port`, `codename`; implemented by a small expression evaluator (no template dependency). A rendered path outside `.nexus/worktrees/` (or, with the sibling layout enabled, outside the repository's parent directory), or into an existing non-worktree directory, is refused unless the operator config allows it.
130	- `list` from one `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` call per worktree plus `rev-list --left-right --count`: dirty, ahead and behind the default branch, integrated (same commit, ancestor, empty three-dot diff, equal tree, patch-id), age, agent marker. JSON schema versioned from day one.
131	- Slash commands `/worktree switch|list|remove` (the existing `/worktree status|merge|discard` keep working), CLI subcommand, sidecar catalogue entry, completion in the TUI, read-only rules, redaction of branch names and paths.
132	- `nexus run --worktree` keeps its behaviour. A new `--worktree-branch <name>` creates a named worktree for the task instead of `nexus/<taskId>` (opt-in, same sandbox requirement).
133	
134	**WP-1311 Shared build caches**
135	- `nexus worktree copy-ignored [--from B] [--to B] [--force] [--dry-run]` and the automatic step in `switch -c`. Source set: files that are both gitignored and listed in `.worktreeinclude`. Default is include-only; the "copy every ignored file" mode needs `--all-ignored` because it can copy `.env` secrets into every worktree.
136	- Implementation: `fs.cp` with `COPYFILE_FICLONE` where supported, `cp --reflink=auto` fallback, plain copy elsewhere; preserve mtimes (so cargo does not rebuild a copied `target/`); skip existing files unless `--force`; exclude `.git`, `.nexus`, `.entire`, nested worktrees; refuse symlinks that leave the tree; cap on count and bytes with a clear error.
137	- Never copy Python virtualenvs (absolute paths); say so.
138	
139	**WP-1312 Merge and clean**
140	- `nexus worktree merge [target] [--no-squash] [--no-rebase] [--no-remove]`: commit (optionally LLM-generated through Nexus's configured provider, never an external command by default), squash, rebase onto target, fast-forward only, then remove the worktree and branch. Back up swept-in working-tree changes to `refs/nexus-backup/<branch>` before squashing. Rebase conflicts stay open in the worktree with a clear message. Uses the existing validation receipt gate (CAND-001..004) when a verifier is configured.
141	- `nexus worktree prune [--dry-run] [--min-age 1d]`: remove worktrees whose branch is integrated, with the minimum-age guard.
142	
143	**WP-1313 Hooks under Nexus's trust model**
144	- Supported events first: `post-start` (after create) and `pre-merge` (blocking). Others later.

The five central source files `agent.ts`, `client.ts`, `parser.ts`, `operation_runner_execution.ts` and evaluator `runner.mjs` had identical local-snapshot and final remote SHA-256 hashes. Evidence: the captured regression file passed 4/4 with the initial uncommitted repairs; the same tests failed 4/4 against the final clean source. Failures cover round-trip recovery state, explicit-null preservation, REPL/sidecar forwarding and ApplicationCore forwarding.
